# 404

*Status code* · also written 404 Not Found

The HTTP status code for a page that does not exist; Google drops such URLs from the index and crawls them less often.

24 claims mention it: 7 from Google's documentation, 9 shown or said at the event (4 confirmed by Google docs, 5 consistent with Google docs), 8 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes).

- [`D1-C102`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Docs: If faceted URLs must be crawled, use the standard & separator, keep filters in a consistent order, and return a 404 when a filter combination has no results. `[D1-C102, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/faceted-navigation]`
- [`D1-C109`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Docs: Google advises against using noindex to save crawl budget and against using robots.txt to temporarily reallocate budget. Use robots.txt only for pages you never want crawled, and 404 or 410 for removed pages. `[D1-C109, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawl-budget]`
- [`D2-C192`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Docs: Google's JavaScript guides say that when client-side routing makes a real 404 status impractical, a single-page app can avoid soft 404s by redirecting with JavaScript to a URL whose server returns 404, or by adding a robots noindex meta tag with JavaScript. `[D2-C192, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics]`
- [`D2-C257`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Docs: Google's JavaScript SEO basics says every page with a 200 status code is queued for rendering, whether or not it uses JavaScript, unless a robots meta tag or header says not to index it; for non-200 pages such as 404 error pages, rendering might be skipped. `[D2-C257, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics]`
- [`D2-C294`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Docs: For client-side rendered single-page apps, where meaningful status codes can be impossible or impractical, Google's documentation gives two ways to avoid soft 404s: a JavaScript redirect to a URL that returns a 404 status, or a noindex robots meta tag added with JavaScript. `[D2-C294, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics]`
- [`D2-C911`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Docs: Google's site move guide says not to redirect many old URLs to one irrelevant destination such as the new site's home page, which can confuse users and might be treated as a soft 404, and to return a 404 or 410 for deleted or merged content that is not moved to the new site. `[D2-C911, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes]`
- [`D3-C673`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Docs: Google's Removals tool help says a temporary removal request usually takes up to a day to process and lasts only about six months, so the content must also be removed permanently, for example with a 404 or 410, a noindex or a password. `[D3-C673, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9689846?hl=en]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C351`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: 404 Not Found and 410 Gone both tell Google there is nothing at the URL, so the URL is not indexable. `[D1-C351, stage, Cherry Prommawin, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C355`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: A soft 404 is a 404 in disguise: the page returns 200 but its content says something like 'page not found', information the site should have sent as the HTTP status. `[D1-C355, stage, Cherry Prommawin, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C190`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: In single-page apps, a missing page often shows a custom 404 page while the server returns HTTP 200, because the front-end router, not the server, handles the 404. `[D2-C190, stage, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C293`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: In an app routed with the History API, when a user reaches a page that does not exist, Erin Sparling suggested asking how they got there and redirecting to a real 404 page. `[D2-C293, stage, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C365`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Google has recently seen more 403 responses to its crawlers (described on stage as 'authentication required'); it treats them as client errors, technically equivalent to 404 or 410, and drops those pages from Search and its AI features. `[D1-C365, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C366`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Google treats a 402 Payment Required response as a 404 Not Found, because Googlebot cannot pay for content. `[D1-C366, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C191`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: The fix for a client-side soft 404 is to make a missing page end with a real HTTP 404 status code instead of 200. `[D2-C191, stage, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C292`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: The fix for a client-side soft 404 is to serve a real 404 error page where appropriate; how to detect URLs that do not exist depends on how the app works and where it is hosted. `[D2-C292, stage, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C639`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: After Google processes a page that now returns a 404 or a noindex, it usually removes the page from its serving index within one to three weeks, sometimes much sooner. `[D3-C639, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C372`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Analysis: Do not answer verified Googlebot with 401, 402 or 403, for example from a login wall, a paywall or a pay-per-crawl setup: Google treats them like 404 and drops the pages, and Google's status code page says not to use 401 or 403 to limit crawling; to slow crawling temporarily, return 429 or 503. `[D1-C372, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D1-C419`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Analysis: A 404 fetch is still a fetch: Google's 2017 crawl budget post says generally any URL Googlebot crawls counts towards a site's crawl budget, so the stage point that 4xx responses do not affect crawl budget is best read as 'they do not slow crawling, and a 404 tells Google to crawl that URL less over time'. `[D1-C419, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C193`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Analysis: In a single-page app, let the server return 404 for unknown routes where possible; otherwise use one of the two client-side fixes Google documents for error views: a JavaScript redirect to a URL that returns 404, or a robots noindex added with JavaScript. `[D2-C193, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C295`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Analysis: After moving to real paths, set the server or hosting rewrite rules so a direct request to every valid path returns 200 with the content (ideally server-rendered) and an unknown path returns a 404 status, which removes client-side soft 404s at the source. `[D2-C295, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C342`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Analysis: Return real error status codes for error states, 404 or 410 for missing content and 503 for outages such as a failed database connection, also in single-page apps; a 200 page whose main content is only an error message is treated as a soft 404 even when header and navigation look normal. `[D2-C342, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C372`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Analysis: Make location and variant pages differ in their main content (local stock, staff, prices, addresses) and return 404 for empty or invalid combinations; otherwise every URL that fits the pattern can be folded into one canonical. `[D2-C372, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C913`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Analysis: For URLs removed in a consolidation, return 404 or 410: Google's site move guide names those two codes, and Google's crawlers treat every 4xx code except 429 the same way, as content that does not exist, so the choice between them matters less than not redirecting to an unrelated page. `[D2-C913, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C653`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Analysis: To hide a URL from Google Search urgently, use the Removals tool in Search Console (about 2 hours) and also add a noindex or a 404, which takes one to three weeks to drop the page from the index. `[D3-C653, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-CAN-10` **MUST** · Documented: Redirect an old URL only to a page with the same intent, and return 404 or 410 when there is none (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-ERR-01` **MUST** · Documented: Return 404 or 410 for removed and non-existent URLs (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-ERR-02` **MUST** · Documented: Return a real 404 for unknown routes in single-page apps, or use a documented client-side fallback (5 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-ERR-03` **AVOID** · Documented: Never serve error states, empty results or failed data loads with a 200 status (2 of its claims mention it)
- `DEV-IDX-13` **SHOULD** · Documented: For an urgent removal, use the Removals tool in Search Console and also return 404 or noindex (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-MON-10` **SHOULD** · Documented: Plan releases and fixes around Google's processing times, and judge results only after them (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SRV-03` **MUST** · Documented: Answer planned maintenance and short outages with 503, for a day or two at most (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SRV-04` **MUST** · Documented: Keep robots.txt reachable on every host: 200 with rules, or 404 if there are none (its own text names it)
- `DEV-SRV-09` **AVOID** · Documented: Do not answer crawlers with 401, 402 or 403 on pages that should be in Search (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-URL-09` **SHOULD** · Documented: If facet URLs must be crawlable, use & separators, a fixed filter order and 404 for empty results (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
